headline: Motion seeking emails on an Apple purchase failed; also approved home education for two students and a sick leave donation.
summary: Staff from the STEM Academy and Lowell High School presented on the Community School Model. Superintendent reports on heating, payroll, and bus cameras were accepted as progress reports. A $200 donation to Morey School and travel requests were also approved.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the November 4, 2026 meeting, 7 yeas.
Approved the Permission to Enter for November 18, 2026, 7 yeas.
Motion to request emails and documents with Apple representatives on a device purchase failed because no one seconded it.
Accepted Superintendent reports 8.1 through 8.9 as reports of progress, 7 yeas.
Approved home education for Shakela Wright and Casandra Heilig, 7 yeas.
Accepted and approved a $200 in-kind donation for the Morey School, 7 yeas.
Bundled and approved the convention and conference travel requests, including Lowell High School travel to Providence, RI and an overnight request to Chatham, MA, 7 yeas.
Approved the donation of fourteen sick leave days to Taylor Leduc, 7 yeas.

Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
LOWELL SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
REGULAR MEETING MINUTES 
, 2025 
 
 
 
Date: November 18, 2026 
Time: 6:30PM 
Location: City Council Chamber, 375 Merrimack Street, 2nd Floor, Lowell, MA 01852 
____________________________________________________________________________________ 
Members of the public can view the meeting via LTC.  Those wishing to speak about a specific agenda 
item must register in advance by emailing the Superintendent.  Please include the agenda item, as well 
as your phone number and email address so we can provide a Zoom link for access. The email address is 
skeo@lowell.k12.ma.us. If you do not have access to email, you may contact us at 978-674-4324. All 
requests must be submitted by 2:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. 
 
1. SALUTE TO FLAG 
 
2. ROLL CALL 
 
On a roll call at 6:32 p.m., members present were, namely: Mr. Bahou, Mr. Conway, Ms. Delrossi 
(Zoom), Mayor Gitschier, Mr. Lay, Ms. Martin (Zoom) and Ms. McFadden.  
 
Mr. Peter Cote, LHS Class Senator was also present. 
3. SPECIAL ORDER OF BUSINESS 
 
3.1. Spotlight on Excellence: Community School Model in LPS 
 
The Spotlight on Excellence highlighted the Community School Model in LPS, celebrating the many 
positive initiatives and opportunities taking place within our community schools. Mr. Hickey of the STEM 
Academy and Ms. Keefe of Lowell High School shared their experiences and insights, emphasizing the 
tremendous impact these programs have on students, families, and the broader school community.  
 
4. MINUTES 
 
4.1. The Approval of the Minutes of the Regularly Scheduled Lowell School Committee Meeting of 
November 4, 2026. 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept and place on file the minutes of the Regularly Scheduled School 
Committee meeting that was held on November 4, 2026; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The 
motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
5. PERMISSION TO ENTER 
 
5.1. Permission to Enter – November 18, 2026 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to approve the Permission to Enter; the motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The 
motion passed with 7 yeas.
(Page 2 of 6) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
6. MEMORIALS 
 
6.1. Sharon Fennelly, Retired Assistant Principal for the Lincoln Elementary School. 
 
7. MOTIONS 
 
7.1. [By Dominik Lay]: Request the Superintendent to provide the whole committee emails, 
correspondence, and communication documents with apple representatives that include and not limit 
to product models that we will be getting, term of price, the $50 discount and the deadline that the 
discount ends, number of the units we are ordering. 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve; the motion was not seconded. The motion fails. 
 
8. REPORTS OF THE SUPERINTENDENT 
 
8.1. Motion Response Update - HVAC Status 
Dr. Hall, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources & Operations, provided the Committee with an 
update from the Facilities Department regarding the progress made in reducing incidents of burst pipes 
and heating system failures. He noted that the school department agrees with the concluding statement 
in the report submitted by the Commissioner of the Department of Public Works to the City Manager 
(that Dr. Hall included) on November 10, 2026, in response to the Mayor’s request for an update. The 
report highlighted that “the city is miles ahead of where the city was four years ago,” noting a significant 
decline in incidents of burst pipes and heating failures over the past several years. As outlined in the 
report, heating plant upgrades have included the installation of freeze-protection measures, which have 
helped prevent frozen coils and pipes. This school year, the district has experienced significantly fewer 
heating-related issues than in previous years. Preventative maintenance and inspections were 
completed on all heating units in September, and parts were ordered as needed to address any required 
repairs. The facilities department looks forward to continuing its collaboration with the City and 
supporting ongoing efforts to secure additional Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) funding 
for further repairs and facility improvements. 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.2. Response To Motion (By Danielle McFadden, 08/19/26 and Mayor Gitschier, 10/21/2026) Regarding 
payroll Schedule outlines. 
Dr. Pinto, Assistant Superintendent for Finance, informed the Committee that the district recognizes the 
financial hardship a gap between paychecks can create for employees who rely on consistent biweekly 
income to meet their household expenses. The district understands the concerns and frustration 
resulting from the circumstances at the start of the school year and acknowledges the importance of 
providing employees with timely and accurate information to help them plan and prepare for changes in 
payroll timing. The anticipated FY26-27 pay gap was communicated to affected personnel on July 29, 
2026.
(Page 3 of 6) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
Moving forward, this information will be shared as soon as the school year calendar is finalized or by 
June 1, whichever occurs first. 
Mayor Gitschier suggested paying less in some of the pay periods so employees do receive a check. 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.3. Response to Motion (Danielle McFadden 10/07/2026) Regarding Exploring a centralized location 
 
Dr. Hall, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources & Operations, informed the Committee that the 
facilities department has been reviewing appropriate spaces for a central facilities location and for a 
central kitchen for over a year. We have studied space on current campuses and what improvements 
would be needed and also looked at properties offered within the City. We have also reviewed 
responses to other RFPs. To date, an appropriate space, given budget constraints, has not been found 
which would be suitable to present as a recommendation to the Committee. In the upcoming SY27 
budget process, Dr. Hall anticipates, given the need for reductions related to decreased student 
enrollment, that we will be able to make other recommendations to the Committee for consideration 
which will address needs identified within this motion. 
 
Mayor Gitschier requested that the Superintendent reach out to the City Manager and inquire about 
utilizing a garage for space needs on Market Street if the city has no use for it. 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.4. Response To Motion (By Fred Bahou, 10/21/26) Explore the possibility of moving 4th and 5th floor 
admin office. 
 
Dr. Hall, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources & Operations, informed the Committee that the 
facilities department has been reviewing potential cost savings proposals related to our expiring facility 
contracts. Given the reduction of enrollment that was projected in the early Fall, we expect the need to 
make cost saving proposals to the Committee after the release of the Governor's budget numbers in late 
January 2027. Several options may include using alternative sites for administrative offices. 
 
Mr. Bahou requested that this motion remain ongoing. 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.5. Response to Motion (By Mayor Gitschier, 10/21/2026) Camera Program on a Selection of School 
Buses 
 
Dr. Hall, Assistant Superintendent for Human Resources & Operations, informed the Committee that he 
and the Director of Transportation have consulted with the Procurement Office as well as
(Page 4 of 6) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
 
communicated with NRT, Inc. related to the path to install cameras on NRT's buses. Currently, the 
district is working on a proposed MOA related to the installation of cameras which would be similar to 
language used in other communities. The report stated that by the next Committee meeting, Dr. Hall 
expects that there should be agreement on the language and hopefully some cameras will be able to be 
installed by the restart of school in early January. 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.6. Quarterly Grants Update, 4th Quarter July 1 - June 30, 2026 (FY26 Q4) 
 
Dr. Pinto, Assistant Superintendent for Finance, informed the Committee that the purpose of presenting 
this grant update to the Committee is to provide an overview of the use and impact of current grants in 
advancing educational initiatives and enhancing school resources. The report covered July 1 to June 30, 
2026 (Q4). 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.7. FY27 Quarter 1 Summary Report 
 
Dr. Pinto, Assistant Superintendent for Finance, provided the Committee a report with a summary of 
FY27 Quarter 1 (through September 30,2026) expenditures across the district. This quarterly update is 
intended to provide a look at spending patterns and resource utilization as compared to the approved 
FY27 General Fund budget. Actual expenditures were approximately 9.6% of the budget, the majority of 
which are payroll related expenses. This percentage is consistent with anticipated early-year spending 
patterns, as instructional staff, who comprise the majority of the budget received their first fiscal year 
pay on September 10, 2026. Some individual areas of the budget show a higher percentage spent or 
committed, such as, pupil transportation at 85.5%, including approximately $15.46 million in 
commitments. These percentages include funds reserved for future costs; they do not mean that all of 
those amounts have already been paid out.  
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.8. State Department Correspondence Summary 
 
Ms. Brown-LeGrand informed the Committee that the Lowell Public Schools received a correspondence 
dated November 9, 2026, from the U.S. Department of State regarding children of Department of State 
employees who have been temporarily displaced from overseas assignments due to security conditions 
in the Middle East. The State Department is asking school districts to consider streamlined enrollment 
pathways for these students and to evaluate, on a case-by-case basis, whether families may qualify for 
protections and services under the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act or another applicable 
emergency enrollment mechanism. In response, Lowell Public Schools will ensure that families 
experiencing temporary displacement have an accessible enrollment process and that McKinney-Vento
(Page 5 of 6) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
eligibility is determined individually based on each family's circumstances. LPS will coordinate with its 
McKinney-Vento, enrollment, and Title I personnel to ensure consistent implementation and 
appropriate support for students and families while continuing to follow applicable federal and state 
requirements. 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.9. Report on Motions 
 
Superintendent Skinner provided the Committee with an updated report on the status of outstanding 
motions and asked the Committee if they had any concerns or questions. 
 
Mr. Bahou inquired about motion M-218 involving ROTC funding for upcoming field trips for 
competitions. 
 
Dr. Pinto stated that monies have been provided and a report will follow at an upcoming meeting. 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 8.1 through 8.9 as 
reports of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
8.10. Home Education 
 
Superintendent Skinner recommended that the following parents/guardians be allowed to home 
educate their child:  
Shakela Wright 
Casandra Heilig 
 
Mr. Conway moved to approve Home Education; the motion was seconded by Mr. Bahou. The motion 
passed with 7 yeas. 
 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
 
9.1. Request to Accept Donation Letter - For Morey School 
 
Morey School will receive an in-kind donation valued at $200 through DonorsChoose. The materials will 
support STEAM activities and challenges integrated into content literacy science instruction. 
 
Mr. Conway moved to accept and approve the donation for the Morey School; the motion was 
seconded by Mr. Bahou. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
10. CONVENTION/CONFERENCE REQUESTS 
 
10.1. Out of State Travel Request - Lowell High School to Providence, RI 
 
Mr. Lay moved to bundle & approve convention/conference requests; the motion was seconded by 
Ms. Delrossi. The motion passed with 7 yeas.
(Page 6 of 6) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
 
10.2. Overnight Request to State Conference - Chatham, MA 
 
Mr. Lay moved to bundle & approve convention/conference requests; the motion was seconded by 
Ms. Delrossi. The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
11. PROFESSIONAL PERSONNEL 
 
11.1. The Members of the United Teachers of Lowell Hereby Donate fourteen [14] Sick Leave Days to 
Taylor Leduc Lowell High School Teacher. 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to approve professional personnel; the motion was seconded by Ms. Martin. 
The motion passed with 7 yeas. 
 
12. ADJOURNMENT 
 
Ms. Martin moved to adjourn at 7:11 p.m.; the motion was seconded by Ms. Delrossi. The motion 
passed with 7 yeas. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Liam Skinner, Superintendent and 
Secretary to the Lowell School Committee
